title: Premature Caching/Memoization of Cheap Computations
pattern: Storing the results of basic arithmetic, bitwise operations, or short memory reads in a hash map or cache to "avoid recomputing."
why_bad: The overhead of hash map key generation, hash computation, bucket collisions, and dynamic allocation is orders of magnitude slower than basic CPU mathematical instructions. A simple add takes < 1 ns, whereas a cache lookup takes 10–50 ns [351, 360, 362].
detection: Introduction of a dictionary or map cache for functions that only perform primitive arithmetic (`+`, `-`, `*`, `/`), basic bitwise logic, or simple struct reads.
counterexample: Caching transcendental math operations (`Math.pow()`, `sin()`, `log()`) or file I/O operations where execution time is genuinely expensive. `Context-dependent`.
